name: data
summary: Load and parse a JSON file from the data directory.
description:
Reads data/<file> and returns the parsed JSON: an object becomes a map you read with .key, an array becomes a list you can range, sort and filter. If the file is missing or invalid, the error is logged and the result is empty.

A page that calls data is rebuilt whenever content changes during -serve.

name: sources
summary: List source files whose property matches a glob.
description:
Returns every source file whose property matches the glob. Properties: Path (public URL), Local (absolute file path), Filename, RelPath (path under src/), Ext, and Meta.<key> for any frontmatter value.

Globs support *, ?, [abc] and {a,b}. * also matches /, so blog/* includes nested files. Each result exposes .Path, .Meta, .LastMod and the other source fields.

Listing pages are dependency-tracked: adding a post rebuilds the pages that list it.

name: sort
summary: Sort sources, JSON objects or key/value pairs.
description:
Works on sources (any property, including Meta.<key>), JSON objects (by a top-level field) and the pairs returned by select (Key, Value, or Value.<field>).

Values are compared as text. Give numbers the same number of digits (05, 10) so they sort correctly. Dates in YYYY-MM-DD form sort naturally.

name: filter
summary: Keep the items whose property matches a regular expression.
description: Takes the same properties as sort and a Go regular expression. Anchor the pattern with ^ and $ for an exact match.

name: limit
summary: Take the first n items of a list.
description: Returns the whole list when it has n items or fewer. Combine it with sort for "latest" lists.

name: offset
summary: Skip the first n items of a list.
description: Returns an empty list when n is past the end. Pair it with limit to feature one item and list the rest.

name: select
summary: Turn a JSON object into a list of key/value pairs.
description: Each pair has .Key and .Value. Map order is random, so sort the result by Key or Value.

name: paginate
summary: Split a list across numbered pages.
description:
Returns the items for the page being rendered and generates the extra pages: a listing at /blog gets /blog/2, /blog/3 and so on. Use it once per page.

Read the position from .Source.CurrentPage and .Source.TotalPages, and build links with pages.

name: pages
description: Returns one entry per page with .Path, .Page (the number) and .Active. The list is empty when everything fits on one page, so the loop renders nothing.

name: page
summary: Generate a page from a template file, once per slug.
description:
Renders the source file (a path under src/) at <its URL>/<slug> and returns that URL. Inside the generated page, .Path holds the slug, which you use to look up the item to show.

A source that uses .Path after a space, as in {{ .Path }}, is a generator: it's only built through page, never on its own. Set path: in its frontmatter to choose the URL prefix. The function pages on this site are generated this way from data/functions.json.

name: path
summary: Prefix a URL with the base path.
description: Joins the -base path and the URL. Write every internal link and asset URL through path and the site works at / and under a subfolder, such as a GitHub Pages project site. Source .Path values already include the base.
example:
<link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ path "/css/styles.css" }}">
<!-- with -base /docs/ this becomes /docs/css/styles.css -->

name: hash
summary: A short content hash of a source file, for cache-busting asset URLs.
description:
Returns the first 10 hex characters of the SHA-256 of src/<file>. Add it to stylesheet and script URLs and browsers fetch a fresh copy when the file changes, and only then. Unlike .BuildID, pages stay byte-for-byte the same between builds when nothing changed, so -publish doesn't upload them again.

It hashes the source file, so for a file with a build: command the hash follows the source, not the command's output. If the file can't be read, the error is logged and the result is empty.

name: json
description: Handy for passing data to scripts, or for writing JSON files from a parse: text template.

name: contains
summary: Check whether a string contains a substring.
description: Note the order: the substring comes first, so it reads well in a pipeline.

name: html
description: SiteGen renders with Go's text/template, which doesn't escape output, so html, js and css return the string unchanged. They exist so templates written for html/template keep working. Only print values you trust.
